subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: RANKED RECOMMENDATION from the run-29 compiler-variant investigation lane. (1) DO NOT SWAP THE COMPILER, and do not spend another lane looking for one. Evidence: claim.law.CV_pinned-residuals-are-unreachable-across-the-local-mwcc-archive.20260901.v1 — 616 fidelity-gated variant compiles over 11 representative TUs spanning every rule class produced ZERO byte-shape reproductions of a pinned target, and the population-scale replay over every TU holding a pure-family residual tested 104 pure-family functions against all 22 archive versions and reproduced EXACTLY ONE. The per-version ledger is the whole argument: the best version in the archive (GC/3.0a3 family) gains 1 exact function and breaks 898; GC/1.3 through 2.7 gain 0 and break ~856; even the near-neighbour revisions GC/1.0 and GC/1.1, which change only 9 and 1 strict functions respectively, gain 0. The melee trade-off is measured, not argued, and it is 1-for-898 at best. (2) TREAT THE CLASS CEILING AS EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED, NOT MERELY ASSUMED. The postprocessor policy requires every class to be attributable to allocator/scheduler variance under a proven compiler. That attribution is now measured: 46 of the 83 pure-recolor residuals induce a well-defined injective register map whose cycle structure is dominated by plain transpositions of CONTIGUOUS register numbers, and one such residual is demonstrably a real MWCC output from a later allocator revision. Progress reporting may now state the EQUIVALENT split's variance origin as allocator-revision variance with a citation instead of leaving it unattributed. (3) THE HIGHEST-VALUE REMAINING POSTPROCESSOR WORK IS A BIDIRECTIONAL LIVE-ZERO PROOF MODE, not more recolor rules. The recolor class is nearly exhausted (78 of 83 pure-recolor functions are already pinned), whereas the live-zero family spans 63 functions and 111 sites of which only 18 rules carry a copy-form stage, and the unserved side is large: the direction split is 56 target-copies/ours-remats vs 55 target-remats/ours-copies, and the shipped equivalent_copy_form class is directional. Roughly half the family has no proof mode at all. The soundness obligation is already written down in claim.law.live-zero-copy-vs-remat-is-allocator-not-source.20260831.v1 (a backward dominating-def scan, a dataflow-equivalence audit class rather than a renaming one), and G3DReadControlPadStates' dominating_def_across_calls mode is the working precedent for crossing a call safely. This is a rule-authoring lane, not a research lane. (4) DO NOT PURSUE p6-STYLE COMPILER DERIVATION FOR EITHER DOMINANT FAMILY. The p6/1.2.5s precedent works because block layout has a LOCAL, UNIQUE candidate: the patch fires only when exactly one candidate satisfies every graph and idempotence proof, and it changed 1 of 94 objects. A register colouring has no such candidate — it is the global outcome of the interference-graph select order, so any heuristic change applies to every function at once and there is no fail-closed uniqueness guard to write. GC/3.0a3's behaviour is the empirical proof of that scope: one function fixed, 33 broken, in a single TU. The live-zero family is structurally more p6-like (one decision at one site), but the near-perfect 56/55 direction split shows there is no single flippable predicate — the same compiler chooses both ways depending on interference state, so a derivation would have to reconstruct the allocator's spill/copy COST MODEL rather than hook a decision point. That is an order of magnitude beyond the block-layout hook, and the WebFrank proof-mode path in (3) reaches the same functions with an already-sound, already-audited mechanism. Estimated scope if attempted anyway: allocator simplify/select/commit plus interference/coalescing/liveness — the frontier the p6 Ghidra import already NAMES but does not patch. (5) PROCESS: retire 'sweep compilers/flags' from future work orders for recolor, permutation and live-zero residuals; cite the law record instead, and use tools/gdl/composed_census/cv_probe.py --axes check if a new TU family's flag identity is ever genuinely in doubt.
